text:
Colorado visits New Jersey tonight, and the model has it close: 3.07 expected goals for COL against 3.02 for NJD. Expected goals measure the quality of chances taken and allowed, and NJD has been better at it, holding 61% of them at five on five against 55% for COL. The Devils create more (3.69 expected goals per 60 minutes to 3.46) while allowing about the same (2.67 against 2.60). On special teams, COL's power play is slightly ahead, at 0.76 expected goals per game to 0.72, but its penalty kill allows 0.39 per game against 0.60 for NJD.

The goalies could swing it. Scott Wedgewood is projected to start for COL, with a backup's workload so far: two games, a .902 save percentage and -0.34 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stopped compared with what the shots called for). Last season he was at +23.58 over 45 games. Jake Allen is projected for NJD at .876 and -2.95 this year, after +5.39 last season. COL is on the second night of a back-to-back, while NJD has had two days off, though the model does not price that rest edge.

Recent form favors the Devils' process. NJD is 3-2-0 in its last five with 61% of the expected goals, and COL is 2-2-1 with 56%. NJD is better than its record, with finishing and goaltending costing it goals. Watch Nathan MacKinnon, who has a 43% chance to score and 86% to record a point, and Jack Hughes at 34% and 72%.
